rationale: No lever value left can realistically pass the gate (needs first-action p50 <=535ms, or quality >0.5455, with premature_transfers <=12). I re-checked DeepSeek V4.1 Flash, the only alternative model that holds up on quality (round 4: 0.538, 6 premature transfers, reverted at 674ms p50). Its round-4 failed-row latency by repeat was r1 885ms (cold start), r2 684ms, r3 640ms, against Gemini at 566-618ms per repeat in rounds 1 and 6, with no warm-up effect. So even warm, DeepSeek is about 60-80ms slower, which still fails the <=635ms latency tolerance; a re-run would very likely revert. Temperature is ruled out (round 6 at 0.0 changed quality by 0.000; 0.7 only risks premature transfers, where any increase reverts the round). The token cap doesn't affect first-action latency and risks truncating tool calls. The gateway route is slower. The GPT/Llama/Qwen families scored speak_and_act=0, and qwen35-122b (more active parameters) is unlikely to beat the 1192ms of Qwen3-Next. For the user: DeepSeek halves premature transfers and raises quality at a cost of about 60-90ms. Relaxing the latency tolerance, or warming the endpoint before scoring, is the decision that would unlock it.
